definition.name: Typed Meta-Relation Operator
definition.definition: A lawful typed relation schema that couples two process expressions across a declared context x without collapsing them into identity.
definition.plain_reading: A and B are interactively related through context x, but remain distinct roles within the relation.

formal_candidate.typed_reading: A is meta-related to B under context x
formal_candidate.admissibility_constraint: A <*>_x B is valid only when the relation preserves distinction, role typing, and admissible continuation.

truth_conditions: A and B are both valid process expressions or projection expressions.
x declares the context/domain of relation.
The relation preserves non-identity between A and B.
The relation produces or constrains at least one admissible projection, coupling, metric, statistical, or closure pathway.
The relation does not erase the upstream distinction structure required by the domain.

⊗.name: Coupling Projection
⊗.reading: A and B are composed or coupled under context x.

⇔s.name: Statistical Projection
⇔s.reading: A and B correspond under statistical projection.

⇔m.name: Metric Projection
⇔m.reading: A and B correspond under metric extraction.

⇔R.name: Residue-Conditioned Closure Projection
⇔R.reading: A and B remain valid through residue-conditioned closure.

examples.reading: Affect and Effect are meta-related under context x while preserving role distinction.
QM_app and GR_app are projection domains related through a typed bridge context without being identified.
Admissibility change and residual delta are coupled under a reorientation/recoupling context.

negative_constraints: <*>_x does not itself prove a bridge.
Family members such as ⊗ must not be treated as isolated primitives.

remove_or_downgrade: Formal ⊗ Coupling Operator as isolated gap
remaining_hardening: Define context typing rules for x.
Define promotion rules for family members.
Define when a <*>_x relation becomes metric, statistical, coupling, or residue-conditioned.
Audit all existing uses of <*>_x, ⊗, ⇔s, ⇔m, and ⇔R for family alignment.
